title: Café de Olla with Piloncillo and Cinnamon
summary: Mexican spiced coffee: water gently warmed with piloncillo, cinnamon, clove and star anise, then steeped with dark-roast coffee and orange peel and strained.
equipment: fine-mesh sieve lined with a coffee filter or paper towel

ingredients.item: piloncillo, chopped, or dark brown sugar

steps.title: Dissolve
steps.text: Put the water, piloncillo (or brown sugar and molasses), cinnamon, cloves and star anise in the pot and warm over medium heat, stirring often, until the sugar has melted. Keep it below a boil, at a bare tremble, for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Steep
steps.text: Take the pot off the heat, stir in the coffee and orange peel, cover and leave for 7 minutes. Steeping off the heat keeps the coffee from turning bitter.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Pour slowly through the lined sieve into a heatproof jug, so the grounds stay behind.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Ladle into mugs while hot. A cinnamon stick in each mug is a nice touch.

tips: Mexican canela (Ceylon cinnamon) is softer and sweeter than cassia.
Grate or chop the piloncillo so it dissolves quickly.
Never let the pot boil once the coffee is in.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat gently without boiling. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
